This alliance will generate research and the development of tools to strengthen SIATA, the Air Quality Monitoring Network, and DAGRD.

At the contract signing ceremony, it was announced that by the end of the year, the metropolitan area will have twelve more air quality monitoring stations, in addition to the eight it currently has.

More and better instruments for monitoring air quality and the risks of natural disasters such as floods and earthquakes. That is one of the objectives of the science and technology transfer agreement signed by EAFIT University and the Metropolitan Area of ​​the Aburrá Valley on the morning of Thursday, May 4th. The agreement includes the installation of air quality monitoring stations in neighborhoods such as Buenos Aires, Aranjuez, and El Poblado.

The new alliance between the two institutions will generate research and development of instruments that will benefit the Early Warning System of Medellín and the Aburrá Valley (SIATA), the Air Quality Monitoring Network, and the Administrative Department of Disaster Risk Management (DAGRD). At the signing ceremony, Juan Luis Mejía Arango, Rector of EAFIT University, expressed his gratitude for the Metropolitan Area's confidence in these types of projects undertaken by the University to fulfill its mission of generating knowledge that contributes to society.

Today, SIATA has eight stations monitoring PM2.5 air pollutants, and by the end of the year, as part of the project, it will have 12 more; six of these in Medellín (in the La América, Buenos Aires, San Cristóbal, El Poblado, Aranjuez, and San Antonio de Prado districts) and the others in the municipalities of Bello, Copacabana, Barbosa, La Estrella, Sabaneta, and Envigado. This was one of the announcements made by Carlos David Hoyos Ortiz, director of SIATA, who also announced that they will be working with researchers from EAFIT University on earthquake monitoring to develop their own instruments.

Eugenio Prieto Soto, director of the Metropolitan Area, emphasized that the contract is very important for the air quality management plan and highlighted the relevance of SIATA not only for the Metropolitan Area but also for the Dagrd (Administrative Department of Risk Management). Camilo Zapata Wills, director of that entity, concurred with this assessment and recalled that SIATA originated in 1999 as a thesis project by Luz Yaneth Mejía, an EAFIT graduate. He also expressed his gratitude for the support of the University's Department of Earth Sciences in the work carried out by that department.

EAFIT, which will manage the SIATA system under this contract, offers—in the words of Rector Juan Luis—the knowledge generated by its researchers on issues such as air quality and risks, thus fostering the application of science to the well-being of society.

"Thanks to SIATA, the Aburrá Valley has been able to develop measurement systems that allow for a better quality of life and preventative measures. This strength is due to an alliance between authorities such as the Metropolitan Area, academia, and the community. Community ownership is crucial, as demonstrated by the network of diverse individuals within the community who are providing real-time information," stated the Rector of EAFIT University, who also expressed the need to transfer this knowledge to other sectors of the country.

Present at the signing and presentation of the contract were Juan Luis Mejía Arango, Rector of EAFIT; Eugenio Prieto Soto, Director of the Metropolitan Area; Camilo Zapata Wills, Director of the Department of Disaster Risk Management (DARGD); Carlos Mario Zuluaga Gómez, Director of the Regional Autonomous Corporation of the Andes (CORNARE); Carlos David Hoyos Ortiz, Director of SIATA; and María del Pilar Restrepo Mesa, Deputy Director of Environmental Affairs for the Metropolitan Area.
